```{r}
data <- read.csv2(file = "C:/Users/Hart/Documents/School/ApplStatMethods/winequality-red.csv", header = T)

nrow(data)
```
# a. What is the sample size?
The sample size for the red wine testing is 1,599.

# b. Any outliers? Do you have any concerns about the data quality?
As tested below, none of the variables contain any missing values.

As shown in the plots, some variables have one or a few outliers, such as volatile acidity. With nearly 1,600 observations, these individual observations should not be a major concern. Several variables are fairly concentrated, while others are more spread out and contain multiple smaller clusters and/or potential outliers.

Based on the information available and the patterns observed in the data, I do not have any major concerns about data quality.

The response variable, quality, is concentrated primarily around ratings of 5 and 6. There are somewhat more observations with ratings of 7 and 8 than with ratings of 3 and 4, but this does not appear to be a major concern. Overall, the data appear suitable for building a model.

```{r}
summary(data)
```
```{r}
# Convert character variables to numeric
data$fixed.acidity <- as.numeric(data$fixed.acidity)
data$volatile.acidity <- as.numeric(data$volatile.acidity)
data$citric.acid <- as.numeric(data$citric.acid)
data$residual.sugar <- as.numeric(data$residual.sugar)
data$chlorides <- as.numeric(data$chlorides)
data$free.sulfur.dioxide <- as.numeric(data$free.sulfur.dioxide)
data$total.sulfur.dioxide <- as.numeric(data$total.sulfur.dioxide)
data$density <- as.numeric(data$density)
data$pH <- as.numeric(data$pH)
data$sulphates <- as.numeric(data$sulphates)
data$alcohol <- as.numeric(data$alcohol)
```

# c. How can you summarize the data of each variable in a concise way? What statistics are you going to present?
I can compare the mean and median of each variable to identify differences in their distributions and potential skewness. I will also present the minimum, maximum, and quartiles to show the range and how concentrated or spread out each variable is.

```{r}
# Example for statistics to present
summary(data$fixed.acidity)
quantile(data$fixed.acidity, p=c(0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9))
```
# d. How can you visualize the distribution of each variable?
In addition to the scatter plots from before, I can use histograms to visualize the distribution and spread of each variable.

```{r}
# Example histogram
hist(data$fixed.acidity, main="Histogram of Fixed Acidity")
```

# e. Do you see any skewed distributions?
While some histograms, such as density, appear fairly normally distributed, several variables, such as alcohol, appear to be right-skewed. I did not observe any variables with an obvious left skew.
